summary: Group all odd-indexed nodes followed by all even-indexed nodes in place.
mainInsight: Keep two pointers, odd (starting at head) and even (starting at head.next), and remember even_head. Repeatedly link odd.next = even.next, advance odd, then even.next = odd.next and advance even. Finally append the even list: odd.next = even_head.

approaches.name: Copy values into two lists
approaches.summary: Rewrite values in the new order.

approaches.name: Two pointers rewiring
approaches.summary: Weave out the odd and even sublists.

commonMistakes: Losing the head of the even list
Using node values instead of positions
Not terminating the even list with None

promptVariants: Which pointers do you need to separate the odd and even nodes?
What must be saved before you start?
options: An odd pointer, an even pointer and the head of the even list
A slow pointer and a fast pointer from the head
A stack of the even nodes to reverse later
A dummy node and a previous pointer only
cards.answer: An odd pointer, an even pointer and the head of the even list
cards.explanation: even_head is attached to the odd tail at the end.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A slow pointer and a fast pointer from t: Those find the middle, not the odd/even split.
incorrectOptionExplanations.A dummy node and a previous pointer only: That does not hold the even list head.

promptVariants: Why is the loop condition `even and even.next`?
What happens at the end of the list?
cards.answer: Each iteration reads even.next and then odd.next, so both even and even.next must exist. When it fails, odd points to the last odd node, so attaching even_head there completes the list.
keyPoints: Odd pointer is the last odd node
cards.explanation: Handles odd and even length lists.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
What does the algorithm do for an empty list or a single node?
options: It returns the head unchanged; a guard avoids reading head.next of None
It creates a new empty even list and returns that
It raises an error since there are no even nodes
It reverses the single node and returns it again
cards.answer: It returns the head unchanged; a guard avoids reading head.next of None
